thinking_text:
**Considering mouse design**

I'm thinking about how to describe an ergonomic mouse design without seams or buttons, which could involve a conceptual approach. I see the need to break down the overall shape into logical sections, like the upper shell, underside, and sidewalls or end caps. It’s interesting to consider how these sections connect, ensuring that they form a contiguous area with functional features, particularly with the scroll wheel. This approach might help clarify the design elements I want to convey!
**Clarifying torus dimensions**

I'm considering the torus center, which has a fixed y, while the bounding box y ranges from 15 to 29. The planar caps have a normal vector in the x direction because of the tilt along the xz plane. The wheel axis is approximately aligned with x, not y, where the normal is also x. So, I think the dimensions should be width in x, vertical in y, and longitudinal in z.
**Considering wheel design**

I'm thinking about the wheel being a separate solid that might be contained within a bracket, but there's no clear axle geometry. It's interesting to ponder if the wheel overlaps in some way or if it's physically separate from other components. I guess the wheel guides motion while being contained in or offset from something larger. There’s a lot of complexity here to explore!

part.name: Ergonomic mouse-style housing with scroll wheel
part.description: A streamlined, bilaterally near-symmetric housing comprising a closed freeform body, an integrated rectangular wheel-support pedestal, and a separate toroidal scroll-wheel solid. The main housing is bounded by six large B-spline surface patches, while the pedestal and wheel use planar and toroidal faces. The STEP model contains 2 solids, 2 shells, and 15 faces.
part.symmetry_note: The main body is approximately bilaterally symmetric about the longitudinal vertical center plane, with closely corresponding left and right flank surfaces. Small differences in the B-spline bounds and the slightly inclined wheel/pedestal geometry prevent exact mirror symmetry. The front-to-rear profile is intentionally asymmetric, with a low tapered nose and a higher rounded rear.

Section.name: Upper ergonomic shell
Section.function intent: Provides the principal hand-contact surface, encloses the upper internal volume, and surrounds the scroll-wheel support interface.
Section.physical behavior: The broad double-curved shell distributes hand pressure over the perimeter and transfers local loads from the wheel-support region into the side and end walls. Its crown curvature increases bending stiffness without requiring ribs.
Section.geometry: One large trimmed B-spline patch spanning the body width and most of its length. It is convex in the transverse direction, rises toward the rounded rear, and slopes downward toward the narrow front. A second trimming wire defines the central pedestal interface.
Section.location: Top of the main body, between the perimeter shell surfaces and above the internal cavity.

major_faces.name: Upper crown surface
major_faces.description: Large upward-facing B-spline shell with a convex ergonomic crown and an inner trimming loop around the wheel-support interface.

Section.name: Lower base panel
Section.function intent: Closes the underside of the housing and provides a broad structural base through which handling and support loads can be transferred to the surrounding perimeter.
Section.physical behavior: The shallow freeform panel acts as a stressed skin. Its curvature resists flexure, while the continuous boundary connection to the perimeter carries bending and torsional loads around the enclosed body.
Section.geometry: A broad downward-facing B-spline patch extending over most of the body planform. It is gently curved rather than perfectly planar and blends into all four perimeter regions.
Section.location: Bottom of the main housing, opposite the upper ergonomic shell.

major_faces.name: Underside base surface
major_faces.description: Large downward-facing, shallow B-spline panel forming the principal underside closure.

Section.name: Peripheral side and end shell
Section.function intent: Connects the upper and lower skins, defines the external footprint, protects the enclosed volume, and forms the rounded gripping and impact-resistant perimeter of the housing.
Section.physical behavior: The continuous perimeter behaves like a closed structural ring. It carries shear between the upper and lower skins, resists torsion, and spreads localized edge or grip loads through the large blended freeform surfaces.
Section.geometry: Four sequentially adjacent B-spline patches forming a closed loop: a high rounded rear end, the left longitudinal flank, a low tapered front end, and the right longitudinal flank. Every patch is smoothly curved and blends into the upper and lower panels.
Section.location: Around the complete outer boundary of the main housing.

major_faces.name: Rounded rear heel
major_faces.description: High, broad B-spline end surface closing the rounded rear of the housing.

major_faces.name: Left flank
major_faces.description: Long freeform left sidewall connecting the rear heel to the tapered front nose.

major_faces.name: Tapered front nose
major_faces.description: Low, curved B-spline end patch closing the narrow front of the housing.

major_faces.name: Right flank
major_faces.description: Long freeform right sidewall returning from the front nose to the rear heel.

Section.name: Scroll-wheel support pedestal
Section.function intent: Provides a rigid mounting and locating structure for the separate scroll wheel while transmitting wheel actuation loads into the main housing.
Section.physical behavior: The narrow box-like tower behaves as a short cantilevered bracket. Its paired sidewalls resist lateral wheel loads, the front and rear walls resist fore-aft loads, and the lower planar face closes the bracket and transfers loads into the surrounding shell.
Section.geometry: A slightly inclined, narrow rectangular pedestal integrated into the main solid. It has two approximately longitudinal side planes, front and rear transverse planes, and one lower horizontal plane. Its upper region intersects the shell and surrounds part of the wheel.
Section.location: Near the longitudinal centerline on the upper-middle region of the housing, below and around the scroll wheel.

major_faces.name: Pedestal left wall
major_faces.description: Large inclined planar wall forming the left side of the rectangular wheel-support tower.

major_faces.name: Pedestal front wall
major_faces.description: Narrow planar wall closing the low-longitudinal or front side of the support tower.

major_faces.name: Pedestal right wall
major_faces.description: Large inclined planar wall opposite FACE 0 and forming the right side of the tower.

major_faces.name: Pedestal rear wall
major_faces.description: Narrow planar wall closing the high-longitudinal or rear side of the support tower.

major_faces.name: Pedestal lower floor
major_faces.description: Planar lower closure of the rectangular support, perpendicular to the housing height direction.

Section.name: Scroll wheel
Section.function intent: Provides a finger-operated rotary interface, nominally for scrolling or incremental input, while remaining located within the central support pedestal.
Section.physical behavior: The toroidal exterior provides a rounded contact tread and converts tangential finger force into torque about the transverse axis. The two planar end regions provide axial limits or potential bearing interfaces, while the pedestal is intended to constrain translation and permit rotation.
Section.geometry: A separate narrow wheel solid with an approximately 14 mm outer diameter and about 5 mm axial width. Its exterior is divided into two toroidal patches, bounded by small planar end faces. The wheel axis runs approximately left-to-right across the housing and is slightly inclined in the longitudinal-vertical plane.
Section.location: Above the upper shell near the centerline, partially contained by the rectangular support pedestal.

major_faces.name: Wheel left end face
major_faces.description: Small planar circular end region on the low-x side of the separate wheel.

major_faces.name: Wheel left toroidal tread
major_faces.description: Toroidal outer patch forming the rounded left portion of the wheel tread.

major_faces.name: Wheel right toroidal tread
major_faces.description: Toroidal outer patch continuing the rounded tread toward the right end of the wheel.

major_faces.name: Wheel right end face
major_faces.description: Small planar circular end region on the high-x side of the separate wheel.
